subject: english-literature
title: Sense and Place
welcome_lead: Smell, sound, touch — settings reach all five senses.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on sensory details that build setting.
final_note: You can now build atmosphere using all five senses.

concepts.def: Image tied to one of the 5 senses.

walkthroughs.body_html: Writers use visual, auditory, olfactory, tactile and gustatory imagery. Weaving more than one builds vivid settings.
Olfactory details ('damp wood and woodsmoke') stir memory powerfully — a quick way to root a reader in place.
Tactile imagery ('icy iron handle', 'velvet bark') makes setting physical — readers feel the world.

mcqs.q: Why distinguish the speaker of a poem from the poet?
options: The speaker of a poem is always the poet themselves.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.
The speaker is the voice constructed in the poem; the poet is the writer. Treating them as identical can mislead, especially with dramatic monologues or personae.
